subject: Production incident: elevated 5xx/429 + retry storm - Silverline Health
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@silverlinehealth.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Reed <ops@silverlinehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: High error rates on /generate -> 5xx/429 burst

Hi Ben,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx responses and a lot of 429s from your API around 07:45 PT. Our patient-facing flows timed out and we had to roll back a deploy locally. We're seeing retries from our side amplifying the issue. Can you confirm if this is an autoscale lag or GPU pool exhaustion on your side? This is impacting our critical morning batch.

I've attached a short support log and a screenshot from our monitoring. Please escalate — we need an ETA.

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Engineering
Silverline Health

Attachments: support-snapshot-20270410.json, client-spans.log
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@silverlinehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 08:22:15 -0700
Subject: Re: High error rates on /generate -> 5xx/429 burst

Elena — thanks for flagging and sharing the logs. I'm escalating immediately. Short summary from our side so you and your team have context: around 07:40 PT we saw a concentrated burst of requests from multiple Silverline hosts that triggered aggressive autoscale activity in the shared hosted pool; autoscaler lagged behind the demand and we observed transient GPU allocation failures which manifested as 5xx bursts and 429s. Additionally, your client's retries appear to be contributing to a retry amplification loop.

Immediate actions we're taking:
- Forcing a short-term capacity increase (+2 burst nodes) into the pool (ETA ~6 minutes).
- Enabling emergency rate-shed for Silverline routes to 60% of normal TPS to break the retry spiral.
- Rolling a fallback to a smaller, less GPU-intensive model variant for your in-flight requests to reduce per-token GPU load.
- Opening a priority incident and looping in platform SRE; Marissa will lead the SRE response.

I'll update you within 10 minutes when the extra nodes are up and we have the first post-fix metrics. Sorry for the disruption — we'll own it.

—Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <elena.park@silverlinehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 08:35:42 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rates on /generate -> 5xx/429 burst

On Sat, Apr 10, 2027 at 08:22 AM ben_carter@redwood.ai wrote:
> Immediate actions we're taking:
> - Forcing a short-term capacity increase (+2 burst nodes) into the pool (ETA ~6 minutes).
> - Enabling emergency rate-shed for Silverline routes to 60% of normal TPS to break the retry spiral.
> - Rolling a fallback to a smaller, less GPU-intensive model variant for your in-flight requests to reduce per-token GPU load.
> - Opening a priority incident and looping in platform SRE; Marissa will lead the SRE response.

Update: burst nodes are provisioning now — I see the new nodes join the pool at 08:41 PT. We recorded a sharp drop in 5xx rate after nodes came up, but we're still seeing elevated latencies on longer contexts while KV cache warms. Metrics attached (sparkline-gpu-metrics.png).

Next steps I recommend (for post-mitigation):
- Work with Silverline to add exponential backoff + jitter on client retries (we can share a patch).
- Schedule a dedicated sizing review (Dedicated pool or committed burst) — current workload pattern shows heavy early-morning batched traffic that benefits from pre-warmed pinned capacity.
- Run a postmortem with timeline and suggested model-quantization adjustments; Markus will draft proposed quantization/packing changes to reduce GPU memory pressure.

Elena: can we schedule a 30-min call today to go over the mitigations and a mutual action plan? Options: 11:00 PT or 14:00 PT.

—Marissa
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: sparkline-gpu-metrics.png
From: Elena Park <elena.park@silverlinehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Reed <ops@silverlinehealth.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rates on /generate -> 5xx/429 burst

Thanks everyone for the quick response and the capacity bump — we saw error rates fall and throughput recover after the nodes came online. Our ops team will implement a client-side backoff patch immediately.

We do want to discuss Dedicated vs Hosted burst patterns: this morning's pattern would have been much less disruptive with a small committed pool or pre-warmed scheduled capacity window. Let's take 11:00 PT today. I'll send a calendar invite.

Action items agreed:
- Redwood: provide incident timeline + metrics + proposed quantization/packing changes (Markus).
- Silverline: roll client retry backoff and share results by EOD.
- Joint: sizing review for a dedicated morning window (schedule on call).

Elena
Director of Engineering, Silverline Health
